title: Reuse a base-item rendering fragment for derived items
goal: Reuse a base-type RenderFragment<T> directly in a derived-item slot within one compatible rendering context. Retain a null policy; generic delegates cannot cross render-mode boundaries.

selectionNotes: Reuse a base-type RenderFragment<T> directly in a derived-item slot within one compatible rendering context. Retain a null policy; generic delegates cannot cross render-mode boundaries.

Keep the generic delegate in one compatible render context. Contravariance does not serialize delegates or permit generic fragments across render modes; blazor.project-static-child-content remains limited to non-generic captured static content.

packageAssets: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components and Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web from the matching shared framework; no external NuGet dependencies or native assets.
platforms: Portable managed renderer harness; Windows x64 execution verified. No native SDK, service account or optional workload.
renderingModes: In-process HtmlRenderer execution; retained HTML output updated on its dispatcher. No browser transport or cross-render-mode execution claimed.
prerequisites: Use the complete project, model, Razor components and Program below. AddLogging supplies HtmlRenderer; the harness does not start a web host.
ASP.NET Core 10 named cascades / typed adapters remain valid comparisons, not a second catalogue edition or a newer API route on net10.0.
constraints: RenderFragment<Observation?> can be used for SpecialObservation? because it accepts every possible derived input. The reverse conversion is unsafe and rejected; .NET 10 requires the typed adapter.
Choose nullable reference inputs deliberately. This template renders a placeholder for null and uses AddContent to encode item text.

Keep the generic delegate in one compatible render context. Contravariance does not serialize delegates or permit generic fragments across render modes; blazor.project-static-child-content remains limited to non-generic captured static content.
stabilityLimitations: Actual evidence: .NET 10.0.13 / SDK 10.0.402 and .NET 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105 / SDK 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105. GA reconciliation and comprehensive publication gates remain open.
